nodes.label: Local PDF and EPUB Build
nodes.rationale: PDF and EPUB are built locally because TinyTeX is slow in CI and print artifacts only need regeneration for tagged releases.

nodes.label: Dual Licensing
nodes.rationale: Code and prose have different reuse needs, following Allen Downey's Think Python arrangement.

nodes.label: Sonic Pi as Laboratory
nodes.rationale: Programming is assumed so each lesson can encode, play, and vary one musical idea.

nodes.label: Syllabus as Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: The generated chapter list and lesson stubs keep the curriculum and published book synchronized.
nodes.norm_label: syllabus as single source of truth

nodes.label: Field Notes Voice
nodes.rationale: First-person field notes preserve the writer's real confusion while second person addresses a specific reader at a keyboard.

nodes.label: Concise Prose
nodes.rationale: Every word without weight is removed and sentence length is varied.

nodes.label: No Encouragement Tone
nodes.rationale: The reader is treated as an adult; interest must come from the sound rather than praise or reassurance.

nodes.label: Executable Sound Claims
nodes.rationale: Every claim about sound must be checkable by running the immediately preceding snippet.

nodes.label: Read-Aloud Lesson Test
nodes.rationale: A lesson becomes tested only after it is read aloud and awkward prose is rewritten; audio recording follows testing.

nodes.label: Generated Chapter Manifest
nodes.rationale: The chapter sequence is generated from the syllabus and must not be edited by hand.

nodes.label: Accessible Syntax Highlighting
nodes.rationale: The a11y theme is selected because Sonic Pi comments carry teaching and must meet WCAG AA contrast.

nodes.label: Incremental Glossary
nodes.rationale: Terms are added as lessons are written so the glossary reflects actual usage.

nodes.label: Edition-Level Provenance
nodes.rationale: A modern edition can carry copyright even when the underlying music is public domain, so the edition must be recorded.

nodes.label: Music Theory Through Sonic Pi Course
nodes.norm_label: music theory through sonic pi course

nodes.label: Sound First, Name Second
nodes.rationale: The reader hears musical structures before receiving terminology.

nodes.label: Music Is Data
nodes.rationale: A note event carries pitch, onset, duration, amplitude, and articulation, and musical transformations operate over those fields.

nodes.label: Score and Renderer Separation
nodes.rationale: Composition data and playback interpretation change independently.

nodes.label: Quarto Toolchain
nodes.rationale: Quarto produces searchable HTML plus PDF and EPUB from Markdown while supporting Lua filters and avoiding a computation engine.

nodes.label: Draft-Test-Observe-Rewrite Loop
nodes.rationale: The author acts as the first student, records confusion before fixing it, and rewrites from field notes.

nodes.label: LilyPond Notation Diagrams
nodes.rationale: Generated SVG notation stays correct, regenerable, and visually consistent.

nodes.label: Publish from Day One
nodes.rationale: Continuous publication makes a partially completed course useful and reduces the all-or-nothing risk.

nodes.label: Programming Is Assumed
nodes.rationale: The book teaches musical theory through representations programmers can inspect, test, and modify instead of reteaching loops and functions.

nodes.label: Sound First, Name Second
nodes.rationale: Intervals, cadences, and modes are heard before their terminology is introduced.

nodes.label: Music Is Data
nodes.rationale: Pitch, onset, duration, amplitude, and articulation form the data model that lessons transform.

nodes.label: Score and Renderer Separation
nodes.rationale: Composition content and playback interpretation should change independently.

nodes.label: Notation Arrives Late
nodes.rationale: Staff notation becomes a decoding exercise after pitch and duration are familiar as numbers.

nodes.label: Confusion Is Data
nodes.rationale: Observations are recorded immediately after an attempt and before edits so the evidence is not destroyed.

nodes.label: Pitch Spelling Field
nodes.rationale: Transcriptions preserve spelling separately from MIDI number because enharmonic names encode musical function and later notation depends on it.

nodes.label: Amplitude, Articulation, and Onset Offset
nodes.rationale: Separating notation from performance lets the same score support strict and expressive renderings.

nodes.label: Sections as Functions
nodes.rationale: Representing sections as reusable functions prevents copy-pasted score data.

nodes.label: Form Assembly from Sections and Transition
nodes.norm_label: form assembly from sections and transition

nodes.label: Printed Note to Sonic Pi Translation
nodes.norm_label: printed note to sonic pi translation

nodes.label: Score Data Before Sound Design
nodes.rationale: Entering the complete score as data before selecting a synth keeps sound design from distracting from decoding.

nodes.label: Source and Licence Inventory
nodes.rationale: Public-domain rules vary by country, and a modern edition of an old work can have its own copyright.

nodes.label: Four-Pass Transcription Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Skipping a pass moves unresolved work into later debugging.

nodes.label: Notation and Interpretation Separation
nodes.rationale: Score facts and performance interpretation must remain separately labelled.

nodes.label: Per-Voice Score Data
nodes.rationale: Separate score structures avoid unsafe shared mutable state across voices.

nodes.label: Voice Separation
nodes.rationale: Changing register, envelope, or panning resolves masking more effectively than volume alone.

nodes.label: Small Transparent Framework
nodes.rationale: A framework large enough to hide the score has failed.

nodes.label: Editable Style Policy
nodes.rationale: Keeping the patterns outside the shell script avoids quoting problems and allows policy edits without code changes.
